gloss: assemble; assembly, a body gathered together
summary: קָהָל is a body of people gathered together, and above all Israel gathered before Yahweh: “the assembly of Yahweh” (Num 16:3; Deu 23:2), which stood at Horeb on “the day of the assembly” to hear his voice (Deu 9:10; 18:16), and was assembled again to keep his feasts, to hear his law read and to praise him (1Ki 8:14, 65; Neh 8:2; Psa 22:23). The same word is a company or host of any kind: armies brought against a city, the company of evildoers, a great multitude of peoples (Ezk 38:15; Psa 26:5; Gen 35:11). The verb is to gather as such a body (niphal), often against someone, and to summon or convene it (hiphil), as the silver trumpets did (Num 10:7). The Septuagint’s ἐκκλησία for קָהָל is the New Testament’s word for the ecclesia, which Stephen uses of Israel at Sinai (Act 7:38).

words.summary: A body of people gathered together and acting as one. Most often Israel assembled before Yahweh, the whole people or those of it summoned; also any company, a host for war, a mob, or the multitude of a people.

senses.gloss: the assembly of Israel, of Yahweh
senses.definition: Israel as one body gathered before Yahweh, “the assembly of Yahweh”, “of God”, “of Israel”: the people that sins and is covered as one, that some may not enter and from which the unclean are cut off.

evidence.note: Korah’s company: “all the עֵדָה are holy, every one, and Yahweh is among them; why then do you lift yourselves up over the קְהַל יַהְוֶה?”
“Why have you brought the קְהַל יַהְוֶה into this wilderness to die there?”
One emasculated “shall not enter the קְהַל יַהְוֶה”: the assembly is a body one belongs to and may be barred from.
No Ammonite or Moabite shall enter the קְהַל יַהְוֶה, “even to the tenth generation … for ever”.
The Edomite’s and the Egyptian’s children of the third generation “may enter the קְהַל יַהְוֶה”.
The law read: no Ammonite or Moabite shall enter בִּקְהַל הָאֱלֹהִים for ever.
The nations have entered her sanctuary, “whom you commanded should not enter your קָהָל”.
If the whole עֵדָה of Israel errs and the matter is hidden from the eyes of the קָהָל: the assembly sins as one.
The bull burned outside the camp: “it is the sin offering of the קָהָל”.
On the day of coverings the high priest covers for himself, his house, “and all the קְהַל יִשְׂרָאֵל”.
“For the priests and for all the people of the קָהָל he shall make a covering.”
The Passover lamb: “all the קְהַל עֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל shall slaughter it between the evenings”.
“The קָהָל: one statute for you and for the stranger who sojourns … as you are, so the stranger shall be before Yahweh.”
One unclean who does not purify himself “shall be cut off from the midst of the קָהָל”.
Korah’s men went down alive to the grave “and perished from the midst of the קָהָל”.
No one to cast the line by lot בִּקְהַל יַהְוֶה: the assembly as the people sharing the inheritance.
“In the sight of all Israel, the קְהַל יַהְוֶה”.
The tribes stood בִּקְהַל עַם הָאֱלֹהִים, four hundred thousand footmen.
“You shall not bring this קָהָל into the land.”

senses.definition: Israel gathered at Horeb to hear Yahweh speak from the fire: “the day of the assembly”.

evidence.note: The tablets bore “all the words Yahweh spoke with you on the mountain from the midst of the fire בְּיוֹם הַקָּהָל”.
The ten words written again, spoken “בְּיוֹם הַקָּהָל”.
What Israel asked “in Horeb בְּיוֹם הַקָּהָל”: not to hear Yahweh’s voice again; so he promises a prophet like Moses (Deu 18:15–18).
“These words Yahweh spoke to all your קָהָל on the mountain … with a great voice.”
Stephen, having quoted Deu 18:15, says Moses “was in the ἐκκλησία in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him in mount Sinai”.

senses.gloss: an assembly convened, for worship, feast or counsel
senses.definition: The people, or their heads, gathered on a given occasion: to keep a feast, to hear the law, to praise Yahweh, to take counsel or make a covenant; the place where praise and testimony are given openly.

evidence.note: At the dedication of the house, Solomon blessed “all the קְהַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, and all the קְהַל יִשְׂרָאֵל stood”.
Solomon kept the feast, “and all Israel with him, a great קָהָל”, fourteen days.
Moses spoke the words of the song “in the ears of all the קְהַל יִשְׂרָאֵל”.
Joshua read every word of the law “before all the קְהַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, with the women and the little ones and the stranger”.
Ezra brought the law “before the קָהָל, both men and women and all who could hear with understanding”, on the first of the seventh month.
“All the קָהָל of those who had returned from the captivity made booths.”
The king, his princes and “all the קָהָל in Jerusalem” took counsel to keep the Passover in the second month.
Many people gathered to keep the feast of unleavened bread, “a very great קָהָל”.
“All the קְהַל יְהוּדָה … and all the קָהָל that came out of Israel, and the strangers” rejoiced.
“All the קָהָל made a covenant with the king in the house of God.”
“All the קָהָל said they would do so, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.”
David: “Now bless Yahweh your God”; and all the קָהָל blessed Yahweh.
“A very great קָהָל of men and women and children” gathered to Ezra as he wept and prayed.
“All the קָהָל answered with a loud voice.”
“All the קָהָל said ‘Amen’ and praised Yahweh.”
“Gather the people, sanctify the קָהָל, assemble the elders, gather the children”, after “blow the shofar in Zion … call a solemn assembly” (Jol 2:15).
The spirit of Yahweh came on Jahaziel “in the midst of the קָהָל”.
“I will declare your name to my brothers; בְּתוֹךְ קָהָל I will praise you”, quoted in Heb 2:12 with ἐκκλησία.
“From you is my praise בְּקָהָל רָב; I will pay my vows before those who fear him.”
“I will give you thanks בְּקָהָל רָב; among a mighty people I will praise you”: קָהָל parallel to עַם.
“I have proclaimed righteousness בְּקָהָל רָב; I have not restrained my lips.”
“I have not hidden your loving-kindness and your truth from the great קָהָל.”
“Let them exalt him בִּקְהַל עָם, and praise him in the seat of the elders.”
“His praise בִּקְהַל חֲסִידִים.”
“The heavens praise your wonders, Yahweh, your faithfulness בִּקְהַל קְדֹשִׁים”: an assembly of holy ones in the heavens.
“I stood up בַקָּהָל and cried for help”: openly, before the gathered people.
Hatred covered by deceit, “its evil shall be revealed בְקָהָל”: before all.
“I was almost in all evil in the midst of the קָהָל and the עֵדָה.”

senses.definition: Those who returned from Babylon, counted and acting as one body: “the assembly of the exile”.

evidence.note: “The whole קָהָל together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty.” Also Neh 7:66.
Whoever did not come within three days “shall himself be separated from the קְהַל הַגּוֹלָה”.

senses.definition: Any large body of people gathered together: a multitude of peoples, a returning throng, an army brought up against a city, the mob that stones, the company of a fallen nation.

evidence.note: To Jacob: “a nation and a קְהַל גּוֹיִם shall be from you, and kings shall come from your loins”.
“That you may become a קְהַל עַמִּים.”
“I will make you a קְהַל עַמִּים, and will give this land to your seed after you.”
Gathered from the north country, the blind and the lame, the woman with child, “a great קָהָל they shall return here”.
Moab of Israel: “Now this קָהָל will lick up all that is round about us.”
Gog’s army: “horses and horsemen, all clothed in full armour, a קָהָל רָב with buckler and shield”.
“You and many peoples with you, all of them riding on horses, a קָהָל גָּדוֹל and a mighty army.”
“You and all your קָהָל that are assembled (הַנִּקְהָלִים) to you.”
“I will raise and bring up against Babylon a קְהַל גּוֹיִם גְּדֹלִים from the north country.”
Pharaoh with “a mighty army and a great קָהָל” will not help him in the war.
Nebuchadrezzar against Tyre “with horses and chariots and horsemen, and a קָהָל and much people”.
“They shall bring up a קָהָל against you, and they shall stone you with stones.” Also Ezk 23:46–47.
“With chariots and wheels, and with a קְהַל עַמִּים.”
Tyre’s mariners and men of war “and all your קָהָל in your midst shall fall into the heart of the seas”.
“I will spread my net over you בִּקְהַל עַמִּים רַבִּים.”
“Asshur is there and all her קָהָל, her graves round about him, all of them slain.”
The women standing by, “a great קָהָל”, who answered Jeremiah in Pathros.
David: “that all this קָהָל may know that Yahweh does not save with sword and spear”: the two armies drawn up.

senses.definition: A company named by those who make it up, good or bad: the assembly of evildoers, of the dead, the council of violent men.

evidence.note: “I have hated the קְהַל מְרֵעִים, and will not sit with the wicked”; against blessing Yahweh בְּמַקְהֵלִים (Psa 26:12).
Of Simeon and Levi: “Into their סוֹד let my soul not come; to their קָהָל let my glory not be united, for in their anger they slew a man.”
“The man who wanders out of the way of understanding shall rest בִּקְהַל רְפָאִים”: the company of the dead.

parallels.note: The congregation; joined with קָהָל in “the assembly of the congregation of Israel”, and set beside it.
“People”: thanks in the great assembly, praise among a mighty people.
“Council”, beside the assembly of Simeon and Levi.
“The seat of the elders”, where praise is also given.

phrases.gloss: the day of the assembly (at Horeb)
a great assembly, a great host

evidence.note: “The ἐκκλησία in the wilderness”: Israel at Sinai, the קָהָל of Deu 9:10 and 18:16, of which Stephen has just quoted Deu 18:15.
Quotes Psa 22:23: “in the midst of the ἐκκλησία I will sing praise to you”.
Set against Sinai (Heb 12:18–21): “the ἐκκλησία of the firstborn enrolled in heaven”.
“On this rock I will build my ἐκκλησία.”
“Tell it to the ἐκκλησία”: the gathered body that hears and judges, and from which one may be put out.

evidence.locator: Gen.28.3, Gen.48.4, Num.10.7, Deu.5.22, Psa.40.11: קָהָל → συναγωγή; ×31 in all (more often for עֵדָה)

evidence.note: “If there come into your συναγωγή a man with a gold ring”: the believers’ own assembly.

words.summary: The verb is not found in the qal. Niphal is to gather as a קָהָל, whether before Yahweh or, often, against someone; hiphil is to make such a gathering, to call the people together, most often to hear Yahweh’s words.

senses.gloss: assemble (before Yahweh, at his house or feast)
senses.definition: Come together as a body at the place or time Yahweh has set: the tent of meeting, his house, the feast.

evidence.note: Moses did as commanded, “and the עֵדָה assembled at the entrance of the tent of meeting”, answering the hiphil of Lev 8:3.
“The whole עֵדָה of the sons of Israel assembled at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there.”
“All the men of Israel assembled to King Solomon at the feast in the month Ethanim, the seventh month.” Also 2Ch 5:3.
“The עֵדָה was assembled as one man, from Dan to Beersheba, to Yahweh at Mizpah.”
On the fourth day they assembled in the valley of Beracah, for there they blessed Yahweh.

senses.definition: Gather as a body to confront someone or to fight: in revolt against Moses and Aaron, against a prophet, or to stand for one’s life.

evidence.note: Korah’s company “assembled against Moses and against Aaron”.
No water, “and they assembled against Moses and against Aaron”.
“When the עֵדָה assembled against Moses and Aaron … the glory of Yahweh appeared.”
When Moses delayed, “the people gathered themselves around Aaron and said, ‘Up, make us gods’”.
“All the people gathered against Jeremiah in the house of Yahweh.”
The whole עֵדָה gathered at Shiloh to go up to war against the two and a half tribes.
The Berites gathered and went after Sheba.
Gog’s host: “all your קָהָל, הַנִּקְהָלִים to you”.
The king granted the Jews “to gather (לְהִקָּהֵל) and to stand for their life”.

stems.gloss: summon an assembly, call together, convene

senses.gloss: call the people together (to hear Yahweh’s word)
senses.definition: Gather the people as a קָהָל before Yahweh, so that they may hear his words, receive his commands or see his work.

evidence.note: At Horeb: “הַקְהֶל־לִי the people, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me.”
At the feast of booths in the year of release: “הַקְהֵל the people, the men and the women and the little ones and your stranger, that they may hear and learn and fear Yahweh.”
“Assemble to me all the elders of your tribes … that I may speak these words in their ears.”
Moses assembled the whole עֵדָה and said, “These are the words Yahweh has commanded.”
“Assemble the whole עֵדָה at the entrance of the tent of meeting” for the priests’ consecration.
“You shall assemble the whole עֵדָה” for the Levites’ setting apart.
“When assembling (וּבְהַקְהִיל) the קָהָל you shall blow, but you shall not sound an alarm”: the silver trumpets that call the עֵדָה (Num 10:2–3).
“Take the rod and assemble the עֵדָה … and speak to the rock before their eyes.”
Moses and Aaron assembled the קָהָל before the rock.
They assembled the whole עֵדָה on the first of the second month and declared their descent.

senses.gloss: summon (the heads of the people, for a national undertaking)
senses.definition: A king calls the elders and heads, or all Israel, to Jerusalem to do something together.

evidence.note: “Solomon assembled the elders of Israel … to bring up the ark of the covenant of Yahweh.” Also 2Ch 5:2.
David assembled all Israel to bring the ark from Kiriath Jearim.
David assembled all the princes and officers to Jerusalem, to charge Solomon with the building of the house.

senses.definition: Gather men into a host to fight, or a faction against a leader.

evidence.note: Rehoboam “assembled all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight”. Also 2Ch 11:1.
“Korah assembled the whole עֵדָה against them at the entrance of the tent of meeting.”
“Have you assembled your קָהָל to take a spoil?”

senses.definition: Of God: to call an assembly, as for a trial, which no one can prevent.

evidence.note: “If he passes through and shuts up, וְיַקְהִיל, who can turn him back?”: Zophar of God bringing a man to account.

parallels.note: “Gather”: Joel’s call to gather the people and sanctify the קָהָל.
Niphal “meet by appointment”: the trumpets gather (נוֹעֲדוּ) the עֵדָה, and assemble (הַקְהִיל) the קָהָל.

words.summary: A rarer form with the same sense as קָהָל, used twice.

senses.definition: A body of people gathered: the assembly of Jacob that holds the law as its inheritance, and an assembly Nehemiah convened against the nobles.

evidence.note: “Moses commanded us a law, an inheritance of the קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב.”
Against the nobles who took interest from their brothers, “I set a great קְהִלָּה against them”: a gathering convened to hear the charge.

words.gloss: Qoheleth: one who assembles, the convener
words.summary: The title by which the son of David, king in Jerusalem, names himself in Ecclesiastes. Its form is the qal participle of the root (feminine, as some titles of office are), “one who assembles”, though the verb is not found in the qal; it takes a feminine verb once and the article once (Ecc 7:27; 12:8). The book does not define it: it shows Qoheleth as a king who “taught the people knowledge”, and Solomon, whose words these are, is the king who assembled Israel and spoke to the קָהָל (1Ki 8:1–2, 14, 55). Whether the title means the one who convenes the assembly or the one who speaks in it, the text does not say.

senses.gloss: the convener, the one who speaks to the assembly (a title)
senses.definition: The name of office of the son of David, king over Israel in Jerusalem, the wise man who taught the people.

evidence.note: “The words of קֹהֶלֶת, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.”
“I, קֹהֶלֶת, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.”
“Because קֹהֶלֶת was wise, he still taught the people knowledge, and weighed and sought out and set in order many proverbs.”
“Vapour of vapours, says קֹהֶלֶת.”
אָמְרָה קֹהֶלֶת, with a feminine verb.
With the article, הַקּוֹהֶלֶת: a title, not a personal name.
Solomon “assembled” (יַקְהֵל) the elders of Israel.
Solomon stood and blessed “all the קְהַל יִשְׂרָאֵל with a loud voice”.

words.summary: Found only in the plural, twice in the Psalms (once with a masculine plural ending, once with a feminine), of the gatherings where Yahweh is blessed.

senses.definition: The gatherings of the people at which Yahweh is blessed: in Psa 68 the procession of singers, players and maidens to the sanctuary.

evidence.note: “My foot stands on level ground; בְּמַקְהֵלִים I will bless Yahweh”, against the קְהַל מְרֵעִים he hates (Psa 26:5).
“בְּמַקְהֵלוֹת bless God, Yahweh, you who are of the fountain of Israel”, after the singers, players and maidens with timbrels (Psa 68:25–26).

opposites.note: The assembly of evildoers, which the psalmist hates, against the assemblies where he blesses Yahweh.

cognates.gloss: (Sabaic) assembly, group; assembly, council of the tribes
cognates.note: Sabaic inscriptions use qhl of “every assembly of enemies” and of “Saba, the community (of associated tribes) in assembly” (gwy qhlm): a gathered body, as קָהָל is, both of a hostile company and of a people as one. A noun qhlt, “assembly, council”, is also listed (Minaean too), matching קְהִלָּה.

evidence.note: “n … qhl(m,n) … (1) ASSEMBLY, GROUP of men or (?) animals … C352/15: kl qhl šnʾm ‘every assembly of enemies’ … (2) specifically, ASSEMBLY, COUNCIL of tribes. C570/9: SBʾ gwy qhlm”.
“ASSEMBLY, COUNCIL (?) … [Cf Heb qehillah = qahal; Min qhl(t+)]”.

cognates.note: The Targum keeps the word where the Hebrew has קְהַל יַהְוֶה (Targ. Onkelos Num 16:3; 20:4). It may have been taken over from the Hebrew of the Torah rather than inherited; it confirms the sense, not the root’s age in Aramaic.

evidence.note: “same [as קָהָל, gathering, congregation]. Targ. Num. XVI, 3. Ib. XX, 4; a. fr. … Pl. קַהֲלֵי”.

cognates.note: Listed with Hebrew qahal under a Proto-Semitic *qhl “assemble”, with the Akkadian sense itself marked uncertain. Not yet checked in an Akkadian dictionary.

evidence.locator: SEM001305 qhl [assemble] V; AKK009371 qaʾālum [gather?] V

doctrine.statement: Israel became the קְהַל יַהְוֶה when Yahweh said “assemble me the people, and I will make them hear my words” and spoke to “all your assembly” from the fire at Horeb (Deu 4:10; 5:22); Moses calls it “the day of the assembly” (Deu 9:10; 18:16). It was a body one could be barred from or cut off from (Deu 23:2–4; Num 19:20), yet the stranger stood in it under one statute (Num 15:15; Jos 8:35), and Jacob was promised that “a company of nations” would come from him (Gen 35:11; 48:4). On that day of the assembly Israel asked not to hear Yahweh’s voice again, and he promised a prophet like Moses (Deu 18:15–18). Stephen quotes that promise and says Moses “was in the ἐκκλησία in the wilderness” (Act 7:37–38), the word the Septuagint used for the קָהָל at Horeb; Hebrews sets the believers’ assembly beside Sinai: “you have not come to the mountain that burned with fire … but to mount Zion … to the ἐκκλησία of the firstborn” (Heb 12:18–23); Jesus says “I will build my ἐκκλησία” (Mat 16:18); and Paul tells the Gentiles that they, once “aliens from the commonwealth of Israel”, are now “fellow citizens with the saints” (Eph 2:12, 19). From the verses: the ecclesia is not a new institution but Yahweh’s assembly carried on, a people called together to hear the prophet like Moses, into which those of the nations are now brought.

The sufferer of Psalm 22, delivered, says “I will declare your name to my brothers; in the midst of the קָהָל I will praise you” (Psa 22:23), and “from you is my praise in the great assembly” (Psa 22:26). Hebrews puts these words in Christ’s mouth: “he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all of one, for which reason he is not ashamed to call them brothers, saying, ‘I will declare your name to my brothers; in the midst of the ἐκκλησία I will sing praise to you’” (Heb 2:11–12), and adds that he shared in flesh and blood like them (Heb 2:14). From the verses: the risen Christ stands among his brothers in the assembly and praises his God with them; he is one of the assembly, not the one it praises in the Father’s place.

The silver trumpets were made “for calling the congregation”: at their blowing the whole עֵדָה gathered at the tent of meeting, and “when the קָהָל is to be assembled you shall blow” (Num 10:2–3, 7); Joel calls for the shofar in Zion to “sanctify the קָהָל” (Jol 2:15–16). Paul says “the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ shall rise first”, and the living with them shall be caught up to meet him (1Th 4:16–17); “the trumpet shall sound and the dead shall be raised incorruptible” (1Co 15:52); and he speaks of “the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to him” (2Th 2:1). From the verses: as the trumpet assembled Israel before Yahweh at the tent of meeting, so at Christ’s return the trumpet raises the dead and assembles his people to him.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Numbers 10 (הַקְהִיל and קָהָל, Num 10:7); Leviticus 23 itself uses מִקְרָא, not this root. Left out as proper names: Kohath קְהָת (s.ap.ai, a person; no name entry written, since this task listed none) with the gentilic קְהָתִי (s.ap.aj), and the wilderness stations Kehelathah קְהֵלָתָה (s.ap.af) and Makheloth מַקְהֵלֹת (s.ap.ah), which are places; whether Kohath is formed from this root is not shown by the text. The database files three keys under this root that are other roots’ words and are left out: s.ap.ak קַו (Isa 28:10, 13 etc., the line/measuring line of קוה), s.ap.am קוֹבַע (helmet, a form of כּוֹבַע), and s.ap.ao קֹוֶה/מִקְוֶה (Kue; the gathering of waters; hope), whose tokens are all spellings of קוה words; also the zero-token cross-references m.df.al and s.bm.ao. The verb has no qal; קֹהֶלֶת is read as its participle. Cognates: Sabaic qhl from Biella’s OCR text only (no PDF renderer available to check the page image). Arabic قهل in Lane (p. 2994) means only “be slovenly in one’s person” and is not a cognate; an Arabic qahala “rebuke” sometimes cited was not found in Lane. Syriac qhal “assemble” is a lead (not in SEDRA’s Peshitta roots; Payne Smith and Brockelmann not consulted). Akkadian qaʾālum is listed only from Anderson–Moser, with their own query; CAD Q not consulted. The Septuagint renders קֹהֶלֶת ἐκκλησιαστής, which the New Testament does not use, so no Greek is given for it. Open questions for review: (1) Psa 89:6 “assembly of holy ones” kept under the worshipping assembly; (2) Job 11:10 hiphil read as God calling to judgment; (3) the doctrine on the trumpet gathering, which joins Num 10 to 1Th 4:16 by theme, not by quotation.
